reading.body:
H.R. 8283 is a Republican-carried bill with two Democratic cosponsors and six lobbying filings naming it, which puts it inside the normal range for AI legislation that industry is watching rather than fighting in public.

The cosponsor list is the clearest signal in the data. Twenty of the twenty-two cosponsors are Republicans, and the two Democrats, Sydney Kamlager-Dove and Josh Gottheimer, sit on opposite sides of the party. A bill tagged to national security and exports that draws that distribution is being built as a security measure first, which is the framing that historically survives committee.

The lobbying side is thin but pointed. The Information Technology Industry Council appears twice, the Software and Information Industry Association once, Meta once, and FDD Action twice. Trade associations filing on a bill usually means members asked them to track it, not that they have taken a position. The blurb is explicit that a filing naming a bill shows the bill was an issue, not the position taken.

What the data does not cover is the bill's substance. There is no text summary, no committee referral, no vote count, and no dollar figure attached to any filing. The status date of 2026-04-15 is the only timing marker, and it says nothing about whether the bill moved. Nothing here connects to compute, buildings, or power, and the record does not support drawing that line.

summary: H.R. 8283, Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026. Latest status date 2026-04-15. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: national security and exports. 6 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
